saints.name: St. Gildas the Wise
saints.title: Monk
saints.shortBlurb: A British monk and historian whose fierce sermon on the ruin of Britain is a chief witness to a lost age…
biography: A British monk born about the year 500, on his own witness in the year of the siege of Mount Badon, Gildas was trained, his later biographer relates, in the monastic school of Illtud in Wales. His surname, Sapiens, 'the Wise', records the fame of his learning in the Scriptures.

His one surviving work, On the Ruin and Conquest of Britain, written about 540, is a sermon in three parts: it mourns the fall of Christian Britain under the pagan Saxons, denounces by name five reigning kings, among them Maelgwn of Gwynedd, and rebukes the clergy of the age. It is almost the sole British voice of its century.

In later life he crossed to Brittany, lived for a time as a hermit on the isle of Houat, and founded the monastery of Rhuys on the Morbihan coast, where he died about the year 570. His feast is kept on 29 January, and his body rests behind the altar of the church that bears his name.
saints.knownFor: His history On the Ruin of Britain.
